title: Context compaction: summarising without losing the essentials

videos.script: A conversation grows until it does not fit, or until it costs more than it is worth. Compaction makes it short. {{summary}} Ask for a summary of Beatriz's first eleven turns in forty words. It keeps the order number and the new address. It drops the one thing an agent needs before writing back: she asked to be written to by email only. {{count}} So count what survives. Six facts an agent must still know, checked in every summary. No summary, at any length, kept all six, and none kept the email. {{pin}} Pin what must survive, word for word: identifiers, and the customer's choices. Summarise the rest. Keep the latest turns as they were. Six out of six. {{rolling}} Summarise a summary, and what the first round kept, the second round drops. {{cut}} And some sentences change meaning when they lose their neighbours: a gift rule, without the word instead. {{end}} A summary is a decision about what matters. Test it like one.
